subject: SIG: follow-up - continuity evidence and failover details

From: Elaine Park <elaine.park@wellnesscorp.com>
To: naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SIG: follow-up on BCDR evidence items

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for taking this on. As part of WellnessCorp's SIG review, our security team asked for a little more color on Redwood's business continuity and disaster recovery coverage. Can you confirm the following?

1) RTO / RPO targets we can reference for hosted inference endpoints (standard tier vs reserved pools).
2) Backup cadence and retention for model artifacts, customer KV caches, and configuration metadata.
3) Cross-region failover: automation vs manual runbook steps, expected time to serve traffic in the secondary region.
4) Any recent rehearsal logs or an abridged runbook we can include in the SIG evidence bundle.

We're trying to close this on our side by EOD Thursday. If you can attach any backup manifests or the current runbook excerpt that would be ideal.

Thanks,
Elaine Park
Security Analyst, WellnessCorp

[Attachment: wellness_sig_request_v2.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
To: Elaine Park <elaine.park@wellnesscorp.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 13:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG: follow-up on BCDR evidence items

Hi Elaine —

Appreciate the clear asks. Summary answers below and I've attached the runbook excerpt + snapshot manifest for your SOC/SIG bundle. If you need formal attestations we can also provide a short signed cover letter.

1) RTO / RPO
- Hosted (standard) endpoints: RTO target 1 hour for degraded read-only; RTO target 4 hours for full write/serve (depends on session state and KV warming). RPO target: 15 minutes for configuration metadata; model artifacts are immutable so RPO is effectively 0 for model binaries.
- Dedicated (reserved pools): RTO target 30 minutes for failover within the same region; cross-region failover RTO target 2 hours. RPO target: 5 minutes for metadata; application-level state depends on customer caching.

2) Backups / retention
- Model artifacts: stored in immutable object storage with versioning; retained for 18 months by default.
- Config and metadata (incl. routing tables, deployment manifests): snapshot every 5 minutes, retained 90 days.
- Customer KV caches: persisted to our snapshot store with a 15-minute cadence; rolling 7-day retention for warm snapshots, longer cold backups on request.

3) Cross-region failover
- Primary: automated failover orchestration can prepare instances in secondary region (KV pre-warming + image pull) automatically when policy thresholds are met.
- DNS cutover is semi-automated: orchestration flips traffic via weighted routing; we prefer a DNS TTL change + weighted routing shift to minimize event windows. Manual approval required by default for customer-managed Dedicated accounts; hosted tier uses auto-fallback policy. Expected time to nominal serve in secondary region: 30–90 minutes for warmed services, up to 2 hours if cold images need to be pulled and caches rebuilt.

4) Rehearsals / runbooks
- Attached: bcdr_runbook_v3.pdf (excerpt), bcdr_snapshot_manifest.csv (example), s3-retention-policy.txt (policy snippet).
- Recent rehearsal: we ran a tabletop + partial failover on 2026-10-15; notes are being collated and we can provide the full rehearsal log under NDA.

Next steps: I can (a) add a short executive summary paragraph for your SIG answers, (b) schedule a quick 30-min Q&A with Vivek (engineering lead for DR) if you want to walk through automation details.

Regards,
Naomi Feldman
Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: bcdr_runbook_v3.pdf (application/pdf)]
[Attachment: bcdr_snapshot_manifest.csv (text/csv)]
[Attachment: s3-retention-policy.txt (text/plain)]

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG: follow-up on BCDR evidence items

Hi Elaine — looping in a couple of technical details that might help with procurement scheduling and your ops runbook. Forwarding Naomi's note inline for context.

> Naomi's note: "1 hour for degraded read-only"

What we mean by degraded read-only: the serving fleet will accept requests but with reduced concurrency limits and higher latency due to cache coldness or partial model shard availability. In practice you may see rate-limits applied to preserve throughput for critical requests. It's not a feature-flagged 'read-only' API, more an operational mode we enforce during partial recovery.

DNS and TTL guidance:
- For customers who control DNS: we recommend keeping a 60s TTL on the inference endpoint CNAME during the onboarding and rehearsal window. That allows rapid weighted-shift if needed.
- For customers who prefer us to manage routing: we can do weighted routing via our traffic gateway with no change to your authoritative DNS, we only require API access to update weightings.

Automation details (brief):
- We pre-pull images and warm KV caches using the snapshot manifest; our orchestration applies initial weighted routing of 5% to secondary region to validate health before ramping.
- Full cutover sequence is documented in bcdr_runbook_v3.pdf, §3.2 and §4.1; rehearsal notes are attached.

If procurement requires a formal rehearsal window, share two preferred dates and we'll propose one.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Customer Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: rehearsal_runbook_notes.md (text/markdown)]
